{"id":"mimid-1wgh.128","title":"Decision needed: the private-use extension key that announces a live call, its CBOR type and its contents","design":"FOR Mark. Bead mimid-1wgh.114.1 says this is the first thing to decide and
that no code should go in before it, so this is the decision bead it asked
for. I have not implemented anything against it.

THE QUESTION. An ordinary message in the PARENT chat announces a live
call: text any client renders ("Alice started a call"), plus a
mimi-content-10 §4.3 extension that a client which knows the key turns
into a Join affordance. Three parts need settling: the key, the value's
CBOR type, and what goes in the value.

1. THE KEY: TEXT, not a negative integer.

§4.3 allows `int / tstr .size (1..255)`, and §8.2.1 says "Negative integer
and text string keys are only for private use". Two implementations
picking private negative integers will collide; two picking text strings
need not. The key is also on the wire where a reader benefits from it
naming itself. mimi-content already models this:
`ExtensionKey::Text(String)`, with MAX_EXTENSION_KEY_LEN 255.

WHICH TEXT, three readings:

(a) a bare word, "liveCall". Shortest. Gives up the only argument for
    text over integers, since another implementation may pick the same
    word and mean something else.
(b) an implementation prefix, "mimid:liveCall". Cannot collide in
    practice, 15 octets.
(c) a tag URI, "tag:reviewcommit.com,2026:mimid:live-call". Cannot
    collide at all, names its owner and its year on the wire, and MATCHES
    THE CONVENTION ALREADY IN THIS CODEBASE: the agent's JMAP capability
    is `tag:reviewcommit.com,2026:mimid:app-passwords`. 41 octets, once
    per call, well inside 255.

MY RECOMMENDATION: (c), for the consistency with what mimid already
spells this way, and because the whole point of the key is to be
unmistakably ours until IANA gives a registered integer. The cost is
octets on one message per call.

2. THE CBOR TYPE: a map.

§8.2.1's registry wants a type for each extension and "encourages a map
containing all the related fields" for related data. A bare text string
holding the room URI would work today and have nowhere to put the second
field we already know we need (see 3).

3. WHAT GOES IN IT. The call room's URI is the one thing a client cannot
proceed without. I would add the media kinds, for a concrete reason found
while building bead mimid-1wgh.114.11: the receiving side projects a
VTCCall from the room, and the room carries no mediaTypes, so that field
is currently EMPTY on every side but the creator's. The announcement is
the only place that information crosses. `subject` has the same problem
and the same fix.

So: { room URI, media kinds, optional subject }. Nothing about keys: the
media secret is fetched, never announced (decision mimid-1wgh.119 and
draft-atwood-jmap-vtc-00 §VTCCall/exportMediaSecret both forbid putting
it in anything pushed).

OPEN SUB-QUESTION I would rather Mark settled: integer or text keys
INSIDE that map. mimi-content's own CDDL is integer-keyed throughout,
which argues integer; but this is a private-use extension whose outer key
is already self-describing text, which argues text for readability. I
lean text, weakly.

4. MARK IT PROVISIONAL, as decision mimid-1wgh.112 did for component id
0xf021: a private-use value, used now, with the draft asking IANA for a
registered one. Bead mimid-1wgh.37.111 is where that ask lives — nothing
in MIMI says a call is live, which is the gap underneath all of this.

AND: no JMAP goes to the MIMI working group (memory
no-jmap-to-the-mimi-wg). This extension is mimi-content, not JMAP, so it
is sayable upstream; the VTC surface that consumes it is not.","status":"open","priority":1,"issue_type":"task","owner":"mark@reviewcommit.com","created_at":"2026-11-25T03:50:34.367711384Z","created_by":"Mark Atwood","updated_at":"2026-11-25T03:50:34.367711384Z","labels":["human","wg"],"dependencies":[{"issue_id":"mimid-1wgh.128","depends_on_id":"mimid-1wgh","type":"parent-child","created_at":"2026-11-25T03:50:34.407592788Z","created_by":"Mark Atwood","metadata":"{}"}]}

{"notes":"DECIDED by Mark, 2026-11-24, all three parts as recommended.

1. THE KEY: the tag URI, reading (c).

     "tag:reviewcommit.com,2026:mimid:live-call"

   A mimi-content-10 §4.3 ExtensionKey::Text, 41 octets, one per call.
   Matches the convention already in the codebase
   (tag:reviewcommit.com,2026:mimid:app-passwords). Cannot collide, and
   names its owner and year on the wire.

2. THE VALUE: a CBOR map, not a bare text string, per §8.2.1's
   encouragement to use "a map containing all the related fields".

3. ITS CONTENTS: room, media, subject.

     room     tstr   REQUIRED   the call room's MIMI URI
     media    array  optional   the media kinds ("audio", "video")
     subject  tstr   optional   the call's subject

   `room` is what a client cannot proceed without. `media` and `subject`
   are there for a reason found building bead mimid-1wgh.114.11: the
   receiving side projects a VTCCall from the room, the room carries
   neither, so both are empty on every side but the creator's, and this
   message is the only place they cross.

   NOTHING ABOUT KEYS. The media secret is fetched, never announced
   (decision mimid-1wgh.119; draft-atwood-jmap-vtc-00
   VTCCall/exportMediaSecret).

4. KEYS INSIDE THE MAP: TEXT, not integers. Mark settled the sub-question
   this bead flagged. mimi-content's own CDDL is integer-keyed throughout,
   which argued the other way, but this is a private-use extension nobody
   can look up: someone reading a capture or a log should not need our
   documentation to tell what they are looking at, and a wrong guess at
   2 versus 3 would be silent. Costs about 15 octets per call.

5. PROVISIONAL, as decision mimid-1wgh.112 was for component id 0xf021: a
   private-use value used now, with the upstream ask for a registered one
   living in bead mimid-1wgh.37.111 (nothing in MIMI says a call is live).
   When IANA assigns an integer key, this text key becomes the legacy
   spelling and both are read for a transition.

IMPLEMENTATION NOTES for bead mimid-1wgh.114.1, which this unblocks:

  - The extension rides an ORDINARY message in the PARENT chat, whose text
    any client renders ("Alice started a video call: standup"). The
    extension is what turns it into a Join affordance. A client that does
    not know the key sees only the text, which is the point.
  - Unknown-field handling is the existing rule: unknown extensions
    round-trip unchanged, and a malformed or oversized one is dropped
    without failing the message (AGENTS.md).
  - `room` must be checked against the sender: a peer-supplied URI must
    not let an announcement point at a room the sender is not in. The
    sender is always the authenticated MLS sender.
  - `subject` and `media` arrive from a peer, so they are data: passed to
    clients, never interpreted, length-capped at parse time with named
    constants.
  - This extension is mimi-content, not JMAP, so it is sayable upstream;
    the VTC surface that consumes it is not (memory
    no-jmap-to-the-mimi-wg)."}

{"notes":"DECIDED by Mark, 2026-11-24, all three parts as recommended.

1. THE KEY: the tag URI, reading (c).

     "tag:reviewcommit.com,2026:mimid:live-call"

   A mimi-content-10 §4.3 ExtensionKey::Text, 41 octets, one per call.
   Matches the convention already in the codebase
   (tag:reviewcommit.com,2026:mimid:app-passwords). Cannot collide, and
   names its owner and year on the wire.

2. THE VALUE: a CBOR map, not a bare text string, per §8.2.1's
   encouragement to use "a map containing all the related fields".

3. ITS CONTENTS: room, media, subject.

     room     tstr   REQUIRED   the call room's MIMI URI
     media    array  optional   the media kinds ("audio", "video")
     subject  tstr   optional   the call's subject

   `room` is what a client cannot proceed without. `media` and `subject`
   are there for a reason found building bead mimid-1wgh.114.11: the
   receiving side projects a VTCCall from the room, the room carries
   neither, so both are empty on every side but the creator's, and this
   message is the only place they cross.

   NOTHING ABOUT KEYS. The media secret is fetched, never announced
   (decision mimid-1wgh.119; draft-atwood-jmap-vtc-00
   VTCCall/exportMediaSecret).

4. KEYS INSIDE THE MAP: TEXT, not integers. Mark settled the sub-question
   this bead flagged. mimi-content's own CDDL is integer-keyed throughout,
   which argued the other way, but this is a private-use extension nobody
   can look up: someone reading a capture or a log should not need our
   documentation to tell what they are looking at, and a wrong guess at
   2 versus 3 would be silent. Costs about 15 octets per call.

5. PROVISIONAL, as decision mimid-1wgh.112 was for component id 0xf021: a
   private-use value used now, with the upstream ask for a registered one
   living in bead mimid-1wgh.37.111 (nothing in MIMI says a call is live).
   When IANA assigns an integer key, this text key becomes the legacy
   spelling and both are read for a transition.

IMPLEMENTATION NOTES for bead mimid-1wgh.114.1, which this unblocks:

  - The extension rides an ORDINARY message in the PARENT chat, whose text
    any client renders ("Alice started a video call: standup"). The
    extension is what turns it into a Join affordance. A client that does
    not know the key sees only the text, which is the point.
  - Unknown-field handling is the existing rule: unknown extensions
    round-trip unchanged, and a malformed or oversized one is dropped
    without failing the message (AGENTS.md).
  - `room` must be checked against the sender: a peer-supplied URI must
    not let an announcement point at a room the sender is not in. The
    sender is always the authenticated MLS sender.
  - `subject` and `media` arrive from a peer, so they are data: passed to
    clients, never interpreted, length-capped at parse time with named
    constants.
  - This extension is mimi-content, not JMAP, so it is sayable upstream;
    the VTC surface that consumes it is not (memory
    no-jmap-to-the-mimi-wg).
SUPERSEDES DECISIONS mimid-1wgh.116 AND mimid-1wgh.124. Mark, 2026-11-24.

HOW THIS BEAD CAME TO EXIST, recorded because the record should not
flatter me: it should never have been filed. Mark had already decided
this question on 2026-11-23 in mimid-1wgh.116 (the key's name and that
its value is a map) and mimid-1wgh.124 (what is in the map), both closed,
and bead mimid-1wgh.114.1's own notes said so in plain text. I filed this
bead from that bead's "FIRST THING TO DECIDE" paragraph without reading
the notes directly below it, and put the question to Mark a second time.
AGENTS.md's "Settled decisions: do not relitigate -- read the relevant
ones before starting work on a bead" is the rule I broke. Told to Mark as
soon as I found it, before any code was written against either answer.

Shown the conflict, Mark chose to let this bead's answers stand. So:

THE KEY IS NOW:

    "tag:reviewcommit.com,2026:mimid:live-call"

superseding "draft-atwood-mimi-calls/call" from mimid-1wgh.116. Both are
private-use mimi-content-10 §4.3 text keys, INVENTED NOT FROM SPEC.

THE MAP IS NOW:

    "tag:reviewcommit.com,2026:mimid:live-call": {
      "room":    "mimi://a.example/r/<call>",   REQUIRED
      "media":   ["audio", "video"],            optional
      "subject": "standup",                     optional
      "ended":   true                           optional, see below
    }

text keys inside, superseding mimid-1wgh.124's "the room's URI and an
ended marker, and nothing else".

WHY MEDIA AND SUBJECT ARE IN, which is the one fact mimid-1wgh.124 did
not have: the receiving side projects a VTCCall from the call room, and
the room carries neither, so both are EMPTY on every side but the
creator's. Found building bead mimid-1wgh.114.11, after .124 was closed.
The announcement is the only place either crosses.

"ended" IS KEPT, and this is MY READING of a supersession Mark did not
spell out, so it is the thing to correct me on. It came from
mimid-1wgh.124, which this bead supersedes, but it is not what the
conflict was about -- the conflict was the key's spelling and whether
media and subject ride along -- and decision mimid-1wgh.117, which STANDS,
refers to "an 'ended' announcement" as part of the settled design.
Dropping it would have changed a decision nobody questioned.

DECISION mimid-1wgh.117 IS NOT SUPERSEDED AND BINDS THIS WORK:

  - The announcement is an INVITATION, not a liveness indicator.
  - Front ends render it as a chat event, NEVER as a live badge.
  - "ended" is ADVISORY: its presence means someone said the call is
    over; its ABSENCE MEANS "NOT KNOWN" and never "still going".
  - Liveness comes from joining the call room. No heartbeat, no presence.

mimid-1wgh.124's warning also carries over and is sharper now that the
map has more in it: extra fields give a client two sources for one fact
and tempt it to infer liveness from the message ("started forty minutes
ago, probably over"). `media` and `subject` are descriptive, not temporal,
which is why they do not reopen that risk -- but the code must not add
anything that is, and must not put the sender or a timestamp in the map,
since both are already the message's.

AN ENDED ANNOUNCEMENT IS A NEW MESSAGE, not an edit of the first
(mimid-1wgh.124's shape note, which survives): an edit is only the
sender's to make, and whoever ends a call need not be whoever started it.

STILL PROVISIONAL, as mimid-1wgh.112 was for component id 0xf021: a
private-use value used now, with the upstream ask for a registered one in
bead mimid-1wgh.37.111."}
